scenario: 面试官问「你会怎么离线评估这个模型？」，你随口报了个团队最熟的指标。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks 'how would you evaluate this offline?' and you name whatever metric your team knows best.
q: 选离线指标该依据什么？选错指标的后果是什么？
q_en: What should the offline metric be chosen by, and what's the cost of picking the wrong one?
why: 指标要匹配三件事：任务类型、数据分布、下游业务目标。指标错配是主要失败模式——一个把「错的离线指标」刷到最高的模型能过离线门却在线上翻车，白白浪费一个 A/B 名额。
why_en: Pick the metric to match task type, data distribution, and downstream business objective; misalignment is a primary failure mode where a model maxing the wrong metric passes the gate but fails online.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  T["任务类型"] --> M["选离线指标"]
  D["数据分布\n(是否不平衡)"] --> M
  B["下游业务目标\n(是否消费概率)"] --> M
  M --> C["分类/排序/回归/生成 + 校准"]
options: 选团队最熟、历史上用得最多的那个指标，与任务和业务无关
匹配任务类型+数据分布+业务目标，错配会线上翻车
永远选 AUC，它是万能指标，任何任务任何分布都能用
选离线分数绝对值最容易做高的那个，分数越高越能说服面试官
options_en: Pick whatever the team knows best and has used most, independent of task or business.
Match task type + data distribution + business objective; misalignment fails online.
Always pick AUC — it's universal and works for any task and any distribution.
Pick whichever absolute score is easiest to inflate; a higher number is more convincing.
optionExplanations: 凭熟悉度选指标正是错配的温床，与任务/业务脱节。
对；三要素对齐才能让离线门真正预测线上，错配是本课的核心警示。
AUC 在严重不平衡下会误导，绝非万能，排序类与回归类都不该用它。
唯分数论会诱导你选一个好刷但与业务无关的指标，正是要避免的。
optionExplanations_en: Choosing by familiarity breeds misalignment, decoupled from task/business.
Correct — aligning the three factors makes the offline gate actually predict online; misalignment is the lesson's core warning.
AUC misleads under severe imbalance and is far from universal; ranking and regression shouldn't use it.
Chasing the score lures you into an easily-inflated but business-irrelevant metric — exactly what to avoid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 选的离线指标与任务/数据分布/业务目标不匹配，模型刷高它却在线上失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metric misalignment is choosing an offline metric that doesn't match the task/distribution/business goal, so a model maxes it yet fails online.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测概率与真实频率是否一致（预测 0.7 应对应 70% 实际发生率），是跨任务的横切属性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration is whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies (0.7 should mean a 70% rate) — a cross-cutting property.

scenario: 信用卡欺诈检测，正例（欺诈）占比不到 1%，你要挑一个离线指标反映「抓到稀有正例」的能力。
scenario_en: Card-fraud detection where positives (fraud) are under 1%; pick an offline metric reflecting how well you catch the rare positive class.
q: 严重类别不平衡的欺诈检测，默认该用哪个分类指标？为什么不用 AUC-ROC？
q_en: For severely imbalanced fraud detection, which classification metric is the default, and why not AUC-ROC?
why: 用 AUC-PR：它只关注稀有正例的 precision-recall，不会被海量真负例（TN）稀释虚高。AUC-ROC 在不平衡下因大量 TN 而虚高——模型几乎全判负也能拿高分。
why_en: Use AUC-PR — it focuses on the rare positive class without inflation from the many true negatives, whereas AUC-ROC looks misleadingly high under severe imbalance.
tradeoff: AUC-PR（聚焦稀有正例、抗不平衡） vs AUC-ROC（阈值无关但被 TN 稀释、不平衡下虚高）
whenOtherWins: 若正负类大致平衡、且你要一个与阈值无关、便于跨模型比较的判别力总览，AUC-ROC 更合适（如内容审核）。
options: AUC-ROC：阈值无关的排序指标，任何分类任务用它都最稳妥
准确率 accuracy：直接看整体判对比例，最直观好解释
AUC-PR：聚焦稀有正例，不被海量 TN 虚高
R²：解释方差比例，衡量分类质量最全面的单一指标
options_en: AUC-ROC: a threshold-agnostic ranking metric, the safest pick for any classification task.
Accuracy: just read the overall fraction correct — most intuitive and easy to explain.
AUC-PR: focuses on the rare positive class and isn't inflated by many TNs.
R-squared: it explains variance, the most comprehensive single measure of classification quality.
optionExplanations: 阈值无关是真，但 1% 正例下海量 TN 会把它抬到 0.99，选它等于自欺。
accuracy 在 1% 正例下把「全判负」也评成 99%，完全失效。
对；AUC-PR 聚焦正例，是 Stripe 欺诈、Gmail 垃圾的默认指标。
R² 是回归指标，不用于分类判别力评估。
optionExplanations_en: Threshold-agnostic is true, but at 1% positives the flood of TNs pushes it to 0.99 — picking it fools you.
Accuracy rates 'predict all negative' as 99% at 1% positives — completely broken.
Correct — AUC-PR focuses on positives and is the default for Stripe fraud and Gmail spam.
R-squared is a regression metric, not for classification discrimination.

termDefinitions.meaning: precision-recall 曲线下面积，聚焦稀有正例、不被真负例稀释，适合不平衡数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC-PR (Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve) focuses on the rare positive class, unaffected by true negatives — ideal for imbalance.

termDefinitions.meaning: ROC 曲线下面积，阈值无关的判别力总览，但在极端不平衡下被大量真负例虚高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC-ROC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is threshold-agnostic discrimination, but inflated by many true negatives under severe imbalance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际为负、也被判为负的样本；不平衡时数量极大，会抬高 AUC-ROC。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A true negative (TN) is an actual-negative correctly predicted negative; hugely abundant under imbalance, inflating AUC-ROC.

scenario: 同一个欺诈模型，AUC-ROC 报 0.95 看着很棒，AUC-PR 只有 0.30。
scenario_en: The same fraud model shows AUC-ROC 0.95 (great) but AUC-PR only 0.30.
q: 为什么在类别不平衡下 AUC-ROC 和 AUC-PR 会给出如此不同的印象？
q_en: Why do AUC-ROC and AUC-PR give such different impressions under class imbalance?
why: AUC-ROC 的假负率分母含海量真负例，模型即便召回很差，FPR 依然很低 → 分数虚高。AUC-PR 的 precision 直接暴露「预测为正里有多少真是欺诈」，稀有正例下这个值很难看。所以不平衡时信 AUC-PR。
why_en: AUC-ROC's false-positive rate is diluted by the huge true-negative pool so it stays high, while AUC-PR's precision directly exposes how many predicted-positives are real, which is harsh under rare positives.
tradeoff: AUC-ROC（被 TN 稀释、乐观） vs AUC-PR（聚焦正例、诚实反映稀有类）
options: 因为 AUC-PR 的计算实现有 bug，二者本应给出完全一致的分数
FPR 被海量 TN 稀释，AUC-ROC 虚高；AUC-PR 更诚实
AUC-ROC 只看正例、AUC-PR 只看负例，所以两者方向恰好相反
两者差异纯属随机噪声，样本多跑几次就会收敛到同一个值
options_en: Because AUC-PR's implementation has a bug; the two should give identical scores.
FPR is diluted by the many TNs so AUC-ROC looks high, while AUC-PR stays honest.
AUC-ROC only looks at positives and AUC-PR only at negatives, so they point opposite ways.
The gap is pure random noise and converges to one value with more sampling runs.
optionExplanations: 两者度量不同侧面，本就不该一致，不是 bug。
对；TN 稀释是 ROC 在不平衡下乐观的根因，PR 用 precision 把真相摆出来。
说反了：AUC-PR 恰恰聚焦稀有正例，不是只看负例。
这是系统性差异不是噪声，重跑不会让它们相等。
optionExplanations_en: They measure different facets and shouldn't match — not a bug.
Correct — TN dilution is why ROC is optimistic under imbalance, and PR's precision surfaces the truth.
Backwards: AUC-PR focuses on the rare positives, not only negatives.
It's a systematic difference not noise; reruns won't equalize them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被判为正的负例占全部负例的比例；不平衡时分母（负例）极大，FPR 易保持很低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FPR (False Positive Rate) is negatives predicted positive over all negatives; under imbalance the huge negative pool keeps FPR low.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测为正里真为正的比例，稀有正例下直接暴露误报有多严重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the fraction of predicted-positives that are truly positive, exposing how bad false alarms are under rare positives.

scenario: Google Ads 用预测 CTR 直接算期望营收来出价，下游把预测概率当真实概率消费，不只是排序。
scenario_en: Google Ads bids using predicted CTR to compute expected revenue; downstream consumes the predicted probability literally, not just ranking.
q: 当下游直接消费预测概率来出价，离线该用哪个分类指标当主指标？
q_en: When downstream consumes the predicted probability to bid, which classification metric should be primary offline?
why: 用 Log loss（交叉熵）：它评的是概率质量而非排序对错，契合概率被当真值消费的出价场景。它对自信却错重罚，逼模型输出可信概率。
why_en: Use log loss (cross-entropy) — it scores the quality of predicted probabilities, not just ranking, fitting a bidding pipeline that consumes probabilities literally, and it heavily penalizes confident-wrong predictions.
tradeoff: Log loss（评概率质量、罚自信错） vs AUC（只评排序、不管概率刻度）
whenOtherWins: 若下游只需要「谁排在谁前面」而不消费概率数值（如纯 top-K 展示），AUC/排序指标就够了，不必上 log loss。
options: AUC-ROC：只要排序对了，出价自然正确
F1：在某个阈值上平衡 precision/recall 即可满足出价需要
Log loss（交叉熵）：评概率质量、重罚自信却错，契合概率被消费的出价
Recall@K：保证召回足够多的广告候选就行
options_en: AUC-ROC: as long as ranking is right, bids are automatically correct.
F1: balancing precision/recall at some threshold satisfies bidding.
Log loss (cross-entropy): scores probability quality and heavily penalizes confident-wrong, fitting bids that consume probabilities.
Recall@K: just ensure enough ad candidates are recalled.
optionExplanations: AUC 只保证相对次序，不保证概率数值准，出价会系统性偏。
F1 是单阈值的分类质量，不评估概率刻度，答非所问。
对；出价把概率当真值，log loss 直接盯概率质量并罚过度自信。
Recall@K 是检索指标，与「概率准不准」无关。
optionExplanations_en: AUC only guarantees relative order, not accurate probability values, so bids drift systematically.
F1 is single-threshold classification quality and doesn't assess the probability scale — beside the point.
Correct — bidding treats probability as truth, and log loss targets probability quality and punishes overconfidence.
Recall@K is a retrieval metric, unrelated to probability accuracy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对数损失/交叉熵：衡量预测概率与真实标签的差距，对自信却错的预测重罚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Log loss (cross-entropy) measures the gap between predicted probabilities and true labels, heavily penalizing confident-wrong predictions.

scenario: 在一个选定阈值上，你同等在意漏报(FN)和误报(FP)，想要一个单一操作点的分数。
scenario_en: At a chosen threshold you care equally about false negatives and false positives and want a single operating-point score.
q: F1 衡量什么？它有哪些盲点？
q_en: What does F1 measure, and what are its blind spots?
why: F1 = precision 和 recall 的调和平均，在一个选定阈值上给单一操作点分数，适合同等在意 FP/FN 的场景。盲点：忽略真负例(TN)、且依赖阈值——换阈值 F1 就变，不能跨阈值比较。
why_en: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall at a chosen threshold, giving one operating-point score when FP and FN matter equally, but it ignores true negatives and is threshold-dependent.
options: 查准/查全（P/R）的调和平均，单阈值、忽略 TN
全阈值上的判别力总览，与阈值无关，天然适合类别不平衡的数据
预测概率与观测频率的一致程度，专门衡量概率刻度是否可信
预测值与真实值的平方误差，回归任务上的标准误差指标
options_en: The harmonic mean of precision and recall at one threshold, ignoring TNs.
A threshold-agnostic overview of discrimination across all thresholds, naturally fit for class imbalance.
How well predicted probabilities match observed frequencies — specifically whether the probability scale is trustworthy.
The squared error between predictions and targets — the standard error metric for regression.
optionExplanations: 对；F1 是单操作点的 P/R 调和平均，代价是无视 TN、且换阈值就变。
阈值无关的是 AUC，不是 F1；F1 恰恰绑定一个阈值。
这是校准的定义，不是 F1。
平方误差是 RMSE/MSE 的回归度量，与 F1 无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — F1 is the harmonic mean of P/R at one operating point, at the cost of ignoring TN and shifting with threshold.
Threshold-agnostic is AUC, not F1; F1 is tied to one threshold.
That's the definition of calibration, not F1.
Squared error is RMSE/MSE for regression, unrelated to F1.

termDefinitions.meaning: precision 与 recall 的调和平均，在选定阈值上给单一分数；调和平均对二者中较小的更敏感。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall at a chosen threshold; the harmonic mean is sensitive to the smaller of the two.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真正例里被找回的比例，衡量漏报(FN)有多少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of actual positives retrieved, measuring how many false negatives you miss.

scenario: 两个模型对一个正样本，A 预测 0.55（对但不自信），B 预测 0.02（自信地错）。
scenario_en: For a positive sample, model A predicts 0.55 (right, unsure) and model B predicts 0.02 (confidently wrong).
q: Log loss 会怎样对待「自信却错」的预测？这对什么系统重要？
q_en: How does log loss treat a confident-wrong prediction, and for which systems does this matter?
why: Log loss 对自信却错重罚——预测 0.02 而真值为正，−log(0.02) 巨大，远超预测 0.55 的惩罚。对把概率当真值消费的系统（广告出价、欺诈拦截决策）至关重要：过度自信会导致系统性错误决策。
why_en: Log loss heavily penalizes confident-wrong predictions (−log(0.02) is huge), which matters for systems that consume probabilities literally, like ad bidding or fraud-block decisions.
options: 轻罚，因为 log loss 只看排序、不看概率数值的大小
重罚：−log(小概率) 巨大，出价系统尤其在意
不罚，log loss 只在类别平衡的数据上才生效
反而奖励自信，鼓励模型输出更极端的概率值
options_en: Lightly, since log loss only looks at ranking, not the magnitude of probability values.
Heavily: −log(small probability) is huge, which bidding systems especially care about.
Not at all; log loss only applies on class-balanced data.
It rewards confidence, encouraging the model to output more extreme probabilities.
optionExplanations: 只看排序的是 AUC；log loss 恰恰盯概率数值。
对；对数惩罚让自信错代价极高，逼模型在消费概率的场景下诚实。
log loss 与类别是否平衡无关，任何概率预测都适用。
恰相反，它惩罚自信错，抑制盲目极端的概率。
optionExplanations_en: AUC is the ranking-only one; log loss targets probability values.
Correct — the log penalty makes confident-wrong extremely costly, forcing honesty where probabilities are consumed.
Log loss is independent of class balance and applies to any probability prediction.
On the contrary, it penalizes confident-wrong, discouraging blind extremes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对错误类别给出接近确定的高概率，log loss 对此施加极大惩罚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Confident-wrong is assigning near-certain probability to the wrong class, which log loss penalizes severely.

scenario: Google/Bing 网页搜索排序，结果有分级相关性（高度相关/一般/不相关），且排在第 1 位远比排在第 10 位有价值。
scenario_en: Google/Bing web-search ranking with graded relevance (highly/partly/not relevant), where position 1 is far more valuable than position 10.
q: 这种带分级相关性、强位置敏感的搜索排序，默认用哪个指标？
q_en: For graded-relevance, position-sensitive search ranking, which metric is the default?
why: 用 NDCG：它支持分级相关性（不只是相关/不相关的二元）并做位置折扣——同一个相关结果排在第 1 位的贡献远大于第 10 位。这正契合搜索排序「靠前的相关结果价值指数级更高」，是 Google/Bing 的默认。
why_en: Use NDCG — it supports graded relevance and position-discounting, so a relevant result at rank 1 counts far more than at rank 10, matching search ranking exactly.
tradeoff: NDCG（分级相关+位置折扣、适合完整排序） vs MRR（只看第一个相关结果、适合单答案查询）
whenOtherWins: 若是导航型查询、只有一个正确答案、你只关心它排多前，MRR 比 NDCG 更贴切、更好解释。
options: MRR：只看第一个相关结果的位置最合适
NDCG：支持分级相关性并做位置折扣，靠前的相关结果权重更高
Recall@K：保证 top-K 覆盖到所有相关结果即可
准确率 accuracy：判对的结果比例最直观
options_en: MRR: looking only at the first relevant result's position fits best.
NDCG: supports graded relevance with position-discounting, weighting earlier relevant results more.
Recall@K: just ensure top-K covers all relevant results.
Accuracy: the fraction of correct results is most intuitive.
optionExplanations: MRR 只看第一个相关项，丢掉了其余位置的分级相关性，不适合完整排序。
对；它同时吃下分级标签和位置折扣，其余排序指标只占其一。
Recall@K 只问「有没有捞到」，不评排序次序质量。
accuracy 不是排序指标，无法反映位置价值。
optionExplanations_en: MRR only looks at the first relevant item, dropping graded relevance at other positions — unfit for full ranking.
Correct — it consumes graded labels and position discounting at once, while the other ranking metrics only do one of the two.
Recall@K only asks whether items were captured, not the ordering quality.
Accuracy isn't a ranking metric and can't reflect positional value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折扣累积增益：分级相关性的排序指标，靠前位置权重更高，归一到理想排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a graded-relevance ranking metric that discounts by position and normalizes to the ideal ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 相关性不是二元而是多级（高度相关/部分相关/不相关），NDCG 能利用这一分级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graded relevance means relevance has multiple levels (highly/partly/not), which NDCG can exploit.

scenario: 导航型/问答型查询，如「Facebook 登录页」或「法国首都」，通常只有一个正确答案，你只关心它排多靠前。
scenario_en: Navigational/QA queries like 'Facebook login' or 'capital of France' usually have one right answer; you only care how high it ranks.
q: 这种「只有一个正确答案」的查询，用哪个排序指标最贴切？
q_en: For 'single right answer' queries, which ranking metric fits best?
why: 用 MRR：它取「第一个相关结果排名的倒数」的平均，正好衡量「唯一正确答案排多靠前」。分级相关性在这里没意义（就一个对的），所以 NDCG 的额外机制用不上，MRR 更简单贴切。
why_en: Use MRR — it averages the reciprocal rank of the first relevant result, exactly measuring how high the single right answer appears, so NDCG's graded machinery is unneeded.
tradeoff: MRR（只盯第一个相关项、适合单答案） vs NDCG（利用整列分级相关、适合多相关结果）
whenOtherWins: 若一个查询有多个不同程度相关的结果、你在意整列排序质量（如商品搜索），NDCG 比 MRR 更合适。
options: Precision@K：看 top-K 里相关比例
NDCG：按分级相关性给整列打分，适合多个相关结果的排序场景
Hit rate：只问 top-K 里有没有相关项
MRR：取第一个相关结果排名的倒数，专测唯一答案排多靠前
options_en: Precision@K: the fraction of relevant items in the top-K.
NDCG: score the whole list by graded relevance — built for queries with several relevant results.
Hit rate: just whether any relevant item is in the top-K.
MRR: the reciprocal rank of the first relevant result, made for how high the single answer appears.
optionExplanations: 只有一个正确答案时，Precision@K 的分子最多为 1，信息量退化，不如直接看排名。
NDCG 的分级相关性是为「多个不同程度相关的结果」设计的；单答案场景没有分级可言，这套机制用不上。
Hit rate 太粗，只答有无、不答排多前，丢掉了关键信息。
对；MRR 的倒数排名正是「唯一答案排多靠前」的自然度量，适合导航/问答。
optionExplanations_en: With one right answer, Precision@K's numerator is at most 1 and degenerates; better to look at rank directly.
NDCG's graded relevance is built for several differently-relevant results; a single-answer query has nothing to grade, so the machinery is wasted.
Hit rate is too coarse — only presence, not how high — losing key information.
Correct — MRR's reciprocal rank is the natural measure of how high the single answer sits, fit for navigational/QA.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均倒数排名：对每个查询取第一个相关结果排名的倒数再平均，衡量唯一答案排多靠前。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank) averages the reciprocal of the first relevant result's rank, measuring how high the single answer appears.

scenario: 两阶段推荐的检索阶段：为一个 top-20 排序器生成 500 个候选，此阶段的成败在于「别把好东西漏在候选集外」。
scenario_en: The retrieval stage of a two-stage recommender generates 500 candidates for a top-20 ranker; success is 'don't drop good items out of the candidate set'.
q: 检索/候选生成阶段该优化哪个指标？
q_en: Which metric should the retrieval/candidate-generation stage optimize?
why: 用 Recall@K（这里 Recall@500）：检索阶段的职责是把所有相关物品都捞进候选集，漏了后面的排序器再强也补不回来。它不在乎候选内部次序（那是排序器的活），只在乎覆盖率。这正是课后测验的答案。
why_en: Use Recall@K (here Recall@500) — retrieval's job is to capture all relevant items into the candidate set, since anything dropped can't be recovered by the ranker; internal order doesn't matter here.
tradeoff: Recall@K（保覆盖、不管次序、检索阶段） vs NDCG/Precision@K（保次序、排序阶段）
whenOtherWins: 若是最终展示给用户的排序阶段、位置和次序决定体验，就该优化 NDCG/Precision@K 而非 Recall@K。
options: NDCG@20：优化候选集内部的排序质量
Recall@500：衡量相关物品是否都被捞进候选集，保证不漏
MRR：只看第一个相关候选排多靠前，衡量排序质量而非候选覆盖
Precision@5：看最前 5 个候选的相关比例
options_en: NDCG@20: optimize the ordering quality inside the candidate set.
Recall@500: whether relevant items are all captured into the candidate set, ensuring nothing is dropped.
MRR: only tracks how high the first relevant candidate ranks — an ordering metric, not a coverage one.
Precision@5: the relevant fraction among the top 5 candidates.
optionExplanations: 排序质量是下游排序器的目标，检索阶段先别丢东西才是首要。
对；Recall@500 直接衡量覆盖率，漏掉的相关项排序器救不回来，是测验答案。
MRR 只盯第一名的位置，回答的是「排得好不好」，检索阶段要回答的是「漏没漏」，问的问题就不对。
Precision@5 是窄窗口的精度，检索阶段的关键是宽召回不是前 5 精度。
optionExplanations_en: Ordering quality is the downstream ranker's goal; retrieval must first not drop items.
Correct — Recall@500 directly measures coverage; dropped relevants can't be recovered — the quiz answer.
MRR only tracks the position of the top hit, answering 'how well ranked' — retrieval needs to answer 'what got dropped', a different question.
Precision@5 is narrow-window precision; retrieval's key is wide recall, not top-5 precision.

termDefinitions.meaning: top-K 候选里覆盖到的相关物品占全部相关物品的比例，衡量检索是否漏掉好东西。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall@K is the fraction of all relevant items captured within the top-K, measuring whether retrieval drops good items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段推荐的第一阶段，从海量物品中快速召回几百个候选交给排序器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is the first stage of two-stage recs, quickly recalling a few hundred candidates from millions for the ranker.

scenario: 两阶段推荐器：检索先从百万物品捞几百个候选，排序器再把候选排成最终列表。
scenario_en: A two-stage recommender: retrieval pulls hundreds of candidates from millions, then a ranker orders them into the final list.
q: 两阶段推荐里，检索和排序各自该优化哪类指标？为什么这样分工？
q_en: In two-stage recs, which metric family does retrieval vs ranking optimize, and why this split?
why: 检索优化 Recall@K（别漏掉好候选，覆盖优先，不管次序）；排序优化 NDCG/Precision@K（把候选排好，次序与位置优先）。分工原因：检索漏掉的东西排序救不回来，而排序质量只在候选集内才有意义。说清这个分工体现架构意识。
why_en: Retrieval optimizes Recall@K (don't lose good candidates, coverage first) and ranking optimizes NDCG/Precision@K (order them well), because dropped candidates can't be recovered and ordering only matters within the candidate set.
tradeoff: 检索：覆盖率(Recall@K) vs 排序：次序质量(NDCG/Precision@K)
diagram:
flowchart LR
  I["百万物品"] --> R["检索\n优化 Recall@K"]
  R -->|几百候选| K["排序\n优化 NDCG/Precision@K"]
  K --> L["最终 top-N 列表"]
options: 检索优化 NDCG、排序优化 Recall@K，先排好次序再保证覆盖
检索优化 Recall@K 保覆盖、排序优化 NDCG 保次序
两阶段都优化 accuracy，指标统一便于横向比较
检索优化 log loss、排序优化 Brier score，都盯概率校准
options_en: Retrieval optimizes NDCG and ranking optimizes Recall@K — get order right first, then coverage.
Retrieval optimizes Recall@K for coverage; ranking optimizes NDCG for ordering.
Both stages optimize accuracy so the metric is unified and easy to compare.
Retrieval optimizes log loss and ranking optimizes Brier score, both targeting calibration.
optionExplanations: 分工反了：覆盖是检索的职责、次序是排序的职责，颠倒会让漏召回无法补救。
对；这个 Recall@K / NDCG 分工正是两阶段推荐的经典架构，点出它体现架构意识。
统一用 accuracy 抹掉了两阶段各自的优化目标，两头都测不准。
log loss/Brier 是校准类指标，不对应检索覆盖与排序次序的分工。
optionExplanations_en: The split is inverted: coverage is retrieval's job and ordering is ranking's; reversing it makes lost recall unrecoverable.
Correct — the Recall@K / NDCG split is the classic two-stage architecture; naming it signals architectural awareness.
Unifying on accuracy erases each stage's objective, mismeasuring both.
Log loss/Brier are calibration metrics, not matching the coverage-vs-ordering split.

termDefinitions.meaning: top-K 结果里相关物品的比例，适合固定 UI 槽位（如 top-5 应用推荐）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision@K is the fraction of top-K results that are relevant, fit for fixed UI slots (e.g. top-5 app recs).

termDefinitions.meaning: 先检索召回候选、再排序精排的架构，两阶段目标不同、指标不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-stage recommender retrieves candidates then ranks them, with different goals and metrics per stage.

scenario: 会话级的粗粒度评估：只想知道推荐列表 top-K 里到底有没有至少一个用户会喜欢的。
scenario_en: A coarse session-level check: just whether the top-K recommendation list has at least one item the user likes.
q: Hit rate 衡量什么？它为什么被称为「粗」指标？
q_en: What does hit rate measure, and why is it called a 'coarse' metric?
why: Hit rate 是二元的：top-K 里是否≥1 个相关物品，命中记 1、否则 0。它粗，因为不管相关项排第几、有几个、相关程度多高，只答「有没有」。适合快速会话级体检，不适合细分排序质量。
why_en: Hit rate is binary — whether at least one relevant item is in the top-K — and it's coarse because it ignores position, count, and grade, answering only presence.
options: top-K 里相关物品的加权分级得分，位置越靠前贡献越大
二元：top-K 里有无≥1 个相关物品，不管位置数量
第一个相关结果排名的倒数，专测唯一正确答案的位置
预测概率与观测频率的一致程度，衡量概率刻度校准
options_en: A weighted graded score of relevant items in the top-K, where earlier positions contribute more.
Binary: whether the top-K holds at least one relevant item, ignoring position and count.
The reciprocal rank of the first relevant result, made for single-correct-answer position.
How well predicted probabilities match observed frequencies — probability-scale calibration.
optionExplanations: 带位置折扣的分级得分是 NDCG，不是 hit rate。
对；hit rate 只问「有没有命中」，是最粗的会话级信号。
倒数排名是 MRR，衡量的是位置而非有无。
概率与频率一致性是校准，不是 hit rate。
optionExplanations_en: Position-discounted graded scoring is NDCG, not hit rate.
Correct — hit rate only asks whether there's a hit, the coarsest session-level signal.
Reciprocal rank is MRR, measuring position not presence.
Probability-frequency agreement is calibration, not hit rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 二元会话级指标：top-K 是否包含至少一个相关物品，粗但直观。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hit rate is a binary session-level metric: whether the top-K contains at least one relevant item — coarse but intuitive.

scenario: 在一个静态基准上把 NDCG@10 提了 5%，上线 A/B 却发现 CTR 没涨。
scenario_en: You raised NDCG@10 by 5% on a static benchmark, but the live A/B shows no CTR lift.
q: 为什么静态基准上的 NDCG 提升可能不转化成在线 CTR？
q_en: Why might a NDCG gain on a static benchmark fail to translate into online CTR?
why: 静态基准常缺 position bias 和会话上下文——真实用户部分是「因为排在前面才点」，基准里没有这个信号。于是你在基准上优化的排序改善，到线上被位置偏置和上下文吃掉，NDCG 涨而 CTR 不涨。这是离线-在线解耦的典型。
why_en: Static benchmarks often lack position bias and session context — users click partly by position — so a benchmark NDCG gain gets absorbed live and doesn't lift CTR.
options: 因为 NDCG 计算错误，用正确算法后一定会转化成 CTR
静态基准缺 position bias 和会话上下文，增益上线被吃掉
因为 CTR 永远和 NDCG 无关，两者根本不应该放在一起看
因为 A/B 的样本量太少，把流量加大到 10 倍后 CTR 自然会涨
options_en: Because NDCG was computed wrong; with the right algorithm it always converts to CTR.
Static benchmarks lack position bias and session context, so the gain is absorbed live.
Because CTR is never related to NDCG and the two should never be looked at together.
Because the A/B sample is too small; scaling traffic 10x would naturally lift CTR.
optionExplanations: 不是算错，是基准本身缺了线上才有的信号。
对；缺 position bias/会话上下文让离线增益不转化，正是两相评估里的解耦案例。
NDCG 本就是 CTR 的离线 proxy，说无关错误。
样本量不解决基准缺失线上信号这个结构问题。
optionExplanations_en: It's not miscalculation; the benchmark lacks signals that only exist live.
Correct — missing position bias/session context makes offline gains not translate — a decorrelation case from two-phase evaluation.
NDCG is precisely an offline proxy for CTR; saying they're unrelated is wrong.
Sample size doesn't fix the structural gap of a benchmark missing live signals.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户部分因结果排位靠前而点击，而非因更相关；静态基准常缺此信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is users clicking partly because a result ranks high, not because it's more relevant — often absent from static benchmarks.

scenario: Uber ETA 预测：想要一个与目标同单位、可直接向业务解释的误差（例如「平均差 2 分钟」）。
scenario_en: Uber ETA prediction: you want an error in the target's own units, directly explainable to the business (e.g. 'off by 2 minutes on average').
q: 要一个可解释、与目标同单位的回归误差，选哪个指标？
q_en: For an interpretable, same-unit regression error, which metric?
why: 用 MAE：平均绝对误差与目标同单位（分钟），「平均差 2 分钟」业务一听就懂。它对每个误差等权、不像 RMSE 那样放大离群点。若偶发大误差代价特别高（如需求预测缺货），才转向 RMSE。
why_en: Use MAE — mean absolute error is in the target's units (minutes), so 'off by 2 minutes' is directly interpretable, and it weights every error equally rather than amplifying outliers like RMSE.
tradeoff: MAE（同单位、可解释、等权误差） vs RMSE（放大离群点、离群代价高时更合适）
whenOtherWins: 若大误差的代价远高于小误差（需求预测大幅低估→缺货、库存崩），要放大离群惩罚，RMSE 比 MAE 更合适。
options: RMSE：平方误差最能压制离群点，最适合 ETA
MAPE：百分比误差跨产品可比，ETA 首选
MAE：与目标同单位、可解释、对误差等权
R²：解释方差比例，最能向业务讲清 ETA 质量
options_en: RMSE: squared error best suppresses outliers, ideal for ETA.
MAPE: percentage error is cross-product comparable, first choice for ETA.
MAE: same units as the target, interpretable, weights errors equally.
R-squared: explained variance best conveys ETA quality to the business.
optionExplanations: RMSE 是放大而非压制离群点，且单位是平方后开根、不如 MAE 直观。
MAPE 是百分比、在真值接近 0 时爆炸，不是同单位可解释的选择。
对；MAE 同单位（分钟）、直接可解释，是 ETA 的自然选择。
R² 是无量纲方差解释比，不能说「平均差几分钟」，解释性差。
optionExplanations_en: RMSE amplifies not suppresses outliers, and its unit is a rooted-square — less intuitive than MAE.
MAPE is a percentage that blows up near zero true values — not the same-unit interpretable choice.
Correct — MAE is in minutes and directly interpretable, the natural ETA choice.
R-squared is a unitless variance ratio and can't say 'off by X minutes' — poor interpretability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均绝对误差：预测与真值差绝对值的平均，与目标同单位、对误差等权。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAE (Mean Absolute Error) averages the absolute prediction errors, in the target's units and weighting errors equally.

scenario: 需求预测里偶尔出现的大幅低估会导致缺货，代价远高于日常小误差。
scenario_en: In demand forecasting, occasional large under-predictions cause stockouts, far costlier than everyday small errors.
q: MAE 与 RMSE 在「对离群误差的敏感度」上有何不同？这决定了什么时候选谁？
q_en: How do MAE and RMSE differ in outlier sensitivity, and how does that decide which to pick?
why: RMSE 先平方再开根，大误差被平方放大 → 对离群点敏感；MAE 线性等权 → 对离群点稳健。所以离群代价高（缺货、大额漏检）用 RMSE 逼模型别犯大错；只要平均水平、离群不特殊贵，用 MAE 更可解释。
why_en: RMSE squares errors so large ones dominate (outlier-sensitive), while MAE is linear and robust; pick RMSE when big errors are especially costly and MAE when you want an interpretable average.
tradeoff: RMSE（放大大误差、离群代价高时选） vs MAE（等权、可解释、离群不特殊贵时选）
options: MAE 对离群更敏感、RMSE 更稳健，所以缺货场景用 MAE
RMSE 平方放大大误差、离群敏感；MAE 等权可解释
两者对离群点敏感度完全相同，只是单位不同而已
RMSE 只能用于分类、MAE 只能用于回归，两者不可混用
options_en: MAE is more outlier-sensitive and RMSE more robust, so use MAE for stockouts.
RMSE squares large errors so it is outlier-sensitive; MAE is equal-weight and interpretable.
Both have exactly the same outlier sensitivity and differ only in units.
RMSE is only for classification and MAE only for regression; the two never mix.
optionExplanations: 敏感度说反了：平方的 RMSE 才对离群敏感，缺货应选 RMSE。
对；平方放大让 RMSE 惩罚大误差，正契合缺货代价高；要可解释均值则 MAE。
平方 vs 线性决定了敏感度不同，并非仅单位差异。
两者都是回归指标，不存在分类专用之说。
optionExplanations_en: Sensitivity is reversed: squared RMSE is the outlier-sensitive one, so stockouts want RMSE.
Correct — squaring makes RMSE punish big errors, fitting costly stockouts; use MAE for an interpretable mean.
Squared vs linear gives different sensitivity, not merely a unit difference.
Both are regression metrics; neither is classification-only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 均方根误差：误差平方求平均再开根，大误差被放大，对离群点敏感。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error) is the root of mean squared errors; large errors dominate, making it outlier-sensitive.

scenario: 你想跨不同量级的产品比较预测误差——有的日销 5 件、有的日销 5000 件，绝对误差不可比。
scenario_en: You want to compare forecast errors across products of very different magnitudes — some sell 5/day, some 5000/day — where absolute error isn't comparable.
q: MAPE 解决了什么、又在什么情况下崩掉？
q_en: What does MAPE solve, and when does it break down?
why: MAPE（平均绝对百分比误差）是尺度无关的，能跨不同量级产品比较——用相对百分比而非绝对量。但真值接近 0 时，除以极小分母会让百分比爆炸/无意义，这是它的崩溃点。
why_en: MAPE is scale-independent so you can compare across product magnitudes via relative percentages, but it breaks down when true values approach zero because dividing by a tiny denominator explodes.
options: 解决离群点敏感的问题，但在数据量太大时会崩掉
尺度无关、可跨量级比较，但真值近 0 时爆炸
解决类别不平衡的问题，但在回归任务上无法使用
让误差与目标同单位，但在跨产品比较时会失效
options_en: Solves outlier sensitivity but breaks down once the dataset gets too large.
Scale-independent for cross-magnitude comparison, but explodes as true values approach zero.
Solves class imbalance but cannot be used on regression tasks.
Keeps error in the same unit as the target but fails for cross-product comparison.
optionExplanations: MAPE 不是为离群设计，也不因数据量大而崩，崩点是真值近 0。
对；尺度无关是它的价值，真值近 0 的除法爆炸是它的软肋。
类别不平衡是分类问题，MAPE 是回归指标，张冠李戴。
同单位是 MAE 的性质；MAPE 恰恰是无量纲百分比、正为跨产品比较而生。
optionExplanations_en: MAPE isn't for outliers and doesn't break on large data; its break point is near-zero truth.
Correct — scale-independence is its value, and division blow-up near zero is its weakness.
Class imbalance is a classification issue; MAPE is a regression metric — a mix-up.
Same-unit is MAE's property; MAPE is a unitless percentage built precisely for cross-product comparison.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均绝对百分比误差：误差占真值的百分比的平均，尺度无关但真值近 0 时失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error) averages the error as a percentage of the true value — scale-independent but breaks near zero.

scenario: 文本摘要任务：要离线评估生成的摘要是否覆盖了参考摘要里的关键信息。
scenario_en: Text summarization: offline-evaluate whether a generated summary covers the key info in the reference summary.
q: 摘要任务的主流自动指标是哪个？它的侧重点是什么？
q_en: Which automated metric dominates summarization, and what does it emphasize?
why: 用 ROUGE：它是召回导向的 n-gram 重叠，衡量「参考摘要里的关键词/短语被生成摘要覆盖了多少」，正契合摘要「别漏掉要点」的诉求，是摘要领域的主流。机器翻译更常用偏精确的 BLEU。
why_en: Use ROUGE — recall-oriented n-gram overlap measuring how much of the reference's key content the summary covers, fitting summarization's 'don't miss the point', and it dominates the field.
tradeoff: ROUGE（召回导向、适合摘要覆盖） vs BLEU（精确导向、适合机器翻译）
whenOtherWins: 若任务是机器翻译、更在意「生成的词有多少确实该出现」（精确度），BLEU 比 ROUGE 更常用。
options: BLEU：精确导向的 n-gram 重叠，摘要任务上的首选
ROUGE：召回导向 n-gram 重叠，衡量要点覆盖
BERTScore：唯一能用于摘要评估的指标，其余都不行
log loss：把摘要当分类任务，用交叉熵来评
options_en: BLEU: precision-oriented n-gram overlap, the first choice for summarization tasks.
ROUGE: recall-oriented n-gram overlap measuring key-point coverage.
BERTScore: the only metric usable for summarization evaluation; nothing else works.
Log loss: treat summarization as classification and score it with cross-entropy.
optionExplanations: BLEU 偏精确、主用于机器翻译；摘要更看覆盖，用 ROUGE。
对；召回导向让 ROUGE 契合摘要「覆盖要点」的目标，是该领域主流。
BERTScore 也可用，但说它是唯一可用是错的；摘要主流仍是 ROUGE。
摘要是生成任务不是分类，log loss 不适用。
optionExplanations_en: BLEU is precision-oriented and mainly for MT; summarization values coverage, so ROUGE.
Correct — recall-orientation makes ROUGE fit summarization's coverage goal and dominate the field.
BERTScore is also usable, but calling it the only option is wrong; ROUGE still dominates summaries.
Summarization is generation not classification, so log loss doesn't apply.

termDefinitions.meaning: 召回导向的 n-gram 重叠指标，衡量生成文本覆盖了参考里多少内容，摘要主流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ROUGE is recall-oriented n-gram overlap measuring how much of the reference the output covers — dominant in summarization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生成文本与参考文本共享的连续 n 个词片段比例，是 BLEU/ROUGE 的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: N-gram overlap is the share of contiguous n-word chunks common to output and reference — the basis of BLEU/ROUGE.

scenario: 生成的句子和参考句意思一致但用了同义改写（'quick brown fox' vs 'fast brown fox'），你要评它质量。
scenario_en: A generated sentence matches the reference in meaning but paraphrases it ('quick brown fox' vs 'fast brown fox'); you must score its quality.
q: BLEU/ROUGE 与 BERTScore 在处理同义改写上有何本质差异？
q_en: What's the essential difference between BLEU/ROUGE and BERTScore on paraphrases?
why: BLEU/ROUGE 靠字面 n-gram 重叠，同义改写（quick↔fast）没有字面重合就被判低分。BERTScore 用上下文嵌入算语义相似度，能识别 quick 与 fast 相近。
why_en: BLEU/ROUGE rely on surface n-gram overlap and penalize paraphrases with no literal match, while BERTScore uses contextual embeddings to measure semantic similarity and catches paraphrases they miss.
tradeoff: BLEU/ROUGE（字面重叠、快但漏语义） vs BERTScore（语义相似、抓改写但更重）
options: 三者都靠字面 n-gram 重叠，BERTScore 只是算得更快一些
BLEU/ROUGE 只看字面，BERTScore 用嵌入抓语义
BERTScore 靠字面重叠、BLEU 靠语义嵌入，恰好相反
三者都能完美评估语义，差别只在计算成本的高低
options_en: All three rely on surface n-gram overlap; BERTScore is merely faster to compute.
BLEU/ROUGE only see the surface form; BERTScore uses embeddings to catch meaning.
BERTScore relies on surface overlap and BLEU on semantic embeddings — exactly reversed.
All three capture semantics perfectly, differing only in how much compute they cost.
optionExplanations: BERTScore 不是字面重叠，它用嵌入算语义，机制本质不同。
对；一个比字符串、一个比向量距离，这决定了改写能不能得分。

BLEU/ROUGE 恰恰抓不到语义改写，不是「都完美」。

Correct — one compares strings, the other compares vector distance, and that decides whether a paraphrase scores.

BLEU/ROUGE precisely fail on semantic paraphrase, so not 'all perfect'.

termDefinitions.meaning: 精确导向的 n-gram 重叠指标，机器翻译标准，被批评忽略语义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) is precision-oriented n-gram overlap, standard for MT, criticized for ignoring meaning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上下文嵌入计算生成与参考的语义相似度，能识别同义改写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BERTScore uses contextual embeddings to measure semantic similarity between output and reference, catching paraphrases.

scenario: 开放式聊天机器人/创意写作，自动指标（BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore）与人类判断相关性都很差。
scenario_en: Open-ended chatbots/creative writing where automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore) correlate poorly with human judgment.
q: 这种开放式生成任务，评估的黄金标准是什么？自动指标的定位是什么？
q_en: For open-ended generation, what's the gold-standard evaluation, and how should automated metrics be framed?
why: 黄金标准是人类评估：开放式生成没有单一参考答案，自动指标与人类判断脱节。面试里应承认自动指标只是 proxy，把人类评估作为校准机制——用人评定期校准自动指标是否还可信。
why_en: The gold standard is human evaluation — open-ended generation has no single reference and automated metrics decorrelate — so frame automated metrics as proxies and use human eval to calibrate them.
tradeoff: 人类评估（黄金标准、贵而慢） vs 自动指标（快但对开放式生成是弱 proxy）
whenOtherWins: 若任务有明确单一参考、答案空间窄（如受限模板生成、机器翻译），自动指标够用，不必每次都上人评。
options: BLEU：开放式生成也能用 n-gram 重叠精确评估
人类评估是黄金标准；自动指标只是 proxy，用人评校准
log loss：把生成当分类问题逐 token 评即可
MAPE：用百分比误差衡量生成质量最稳妥
options_en: BLEU: open-ended generation can be precisely scored by n-gram overlap too.
Human evaluation is the gold standard; automated metrics are proxies to be calibrated by human eval.
Log loss: treat generation as classification and score per-token.
MAPE: percentage error most reliably measures generation quality.
optionExplanations: 开放式生成没有单一参考，BLEU 的字面重叠与人类判断脱节。
对；人评是黄金标准，自动指标当 proxy 并靠人评校准，是面试该说的定位。
逐 token log loss 测的是语言模型拟合，不等于开放式生成质量。
MAPE 是回归百分比误差，与文本生成质量无关。
optionExplanations_en: Open-ended generation has no single reference, so BLEU's surface overlap decorrelates from human judgment.
Correct — human eval is the gold standard, with automated metrics as proxies calibrated by it — the framing to state.
Per-token log loss measures language-model fit, not open-ended generation quality.
MAPE is regression percentage error, unrelated to text-generation quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由人对开放式生成质量打分/比较，是自动指标失效场景的黄金标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Human evaluation is people scoring/comparing open-ended generation quality — the gold standard where automated metrics fail.

scenario: 一个模型对一批样本预测「0.7 概率是欺诈」，下游要把这 0.7 当真实概率去算期望损失。
scenario_en: A model predicts '0.7 probability of fraud' for a batch, and downstream treats 0.7 as the true probability to compute expected loss.
q: 「模型校准良好」具体指什么？什么时候校准才重要？
q_en: What exactly does 'well-calibrated' mean, and when does calibration matter?
why: 校准良好 = 预测概率与观测频率一致：所有被预测为 0.7 的样本里，实际约 70% 真的是正例。只要下游把概率当真值字面消费（出价、期望损失、拦截阈值），校准就重要；若只用排序、不看概率数值，则不重要。
why_en: Well-calibrated means predicted probabilities match observed frequencies — among items predicted 0.7, about 70% are truly positive — and it matters whenever probabilities are consumed literally.
options: 指模型的排序能力强，AUC 高就等于校准良好
预测概率=观测频率（0.7→约 70% 为正）
指模型对所有样本都输出同一个概率，方差为 0
指训练 loss 收敛到 0，训练足够充分就是校准好
options_en: It means the model ranks well; a high AUC is the same as being well-calibrated.
Predicted probability equals observed frequency (0.7 → about 70% turn out positive).
It means the model outputs the same probability for every sample, with zero variance.
It means training loss converged to 0; training long enough is what calibration means.
optionExplanations: AUC 只管排序，校准好坏与 AUC 高低可以完全脱钩。
对；校准是概率与频率对齐，只有下游消费概率数值时才关键。
同一概率不是校准，是退化的常数预测。
训练 loss 收敛不保证概率刻度准，校准是另一回事。
optionExplanations_en: AUC only concerns ranking and can fully decouple from calibration.
Correct — calibration aligns probability with frequency, crucial only when downstream consumes probability values.
One constant probability isn't calibration; it's a degenerate constant prediction.
Converged training loss doesn't guarantee an accurate probability scale — calibration is separate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测概率 p 的样本里，真实正例比例约等于 p，概率可被当真值使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Well-calibrated means among items predicted probability p, about p of them are truly positive, so the probability is usable as truth.

scenario: 广告排序用预测 CTR × 出价算期望营收来竞价；若预测 CTR 系统性偏高，就会过度出价、亏钱。
scenario_en: Ad ranking bids using predicted CTR × bid to compute expected revenue; if predicted CTR is systematically too high, you overbid and lose money.
q: 对广告出价系统，除了 AUC 这类排序指标，为什么必须检查校准？
q_en: For an ad-bidding system, why must you check calibration beyond ranking metrics like AUC?
why: 出价把预测 CTR 当真实概率乘进期望营收，概率数值直接决定钱。AUC 只保证「谁比谁点击率高」的排序，保证不了「0.7 就真是 70%」；若系统性高估，AUC 再好也会过度出价亏钱。所以必须在主指标之外查校准（Brier/可靠性图）。
why_en: Bidding multiplies predicted CTR into expected revenue, so the probability value directly sets the money; AUC only guarantees ranking, not that 0.7 means 70%, so overconfidence overbids and loses money.
tradeoff: 只看 AUC（保排序、不保概率刻度） vs 加查校准（保 0.7≈70%，出价才不亏）
whenOtherWins: 若系统只按预测分数排序展示、从不把概率乘进金额或阈值决策，那么排序指标就够，校准不是必需。
options: 不必查校准，AUC 高就代表出价一定正确
CTR 被当真值乘进营收，AUC 保排序不保刻度
只需查 recall，保证召回到足够多的广告候选即可
校准只对图像任务有意义，广告 CTR 场景无关
options_en: No need to check calibration; a high AUC means the bids must be correct.
CTR is multiplied into revenue as truth, and AUC guarantees ranking, not the scale.
Just check recall — recalling enough ad candidates is all that's needed.
Calibration only matters for image tasks and is irrelevant to ad CTR.
optionExplanations: AUC 高但概率系统性偏高照样过度出价，排序对≠概率准。
对；钱由概率数值决定，必须在 AUC 之外查校准才不会系统性亏钱。
recall 是覆盖指标，与「概率数值准不准导致的出价对错」无关。
校准对任何消费概率的系统都重要，广告 CTR 正是典型。
optionExplanations_en: High AUC with systematically inflated probabilities still overbids; correct ranking isn't accurate probability.
Correct — money is set by the probability value, so you must check calibration beyond AUC to avoid systematic losses.
Recall is a coverage metric, unrelated to bid correctness driven by probability accuracy.
Calibration matters for any probability-consuming system; ad CTR is the textbook case.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测点击率乘以出价（及价值），概率偏差会直接放大成金钱损益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Expected revenue is predicted CTR times bid/value; probability bias scales directly into monetary gain or loss.

scenario: 模型在漂移后的数据上重训，AUC 依旧稳定，但预测概率系统性偏离真实频率。
scenario_en: A model retrained on shifted data keeps a stable AUC, but its predicted probabilities systematically drift from true frequencies.
q: 为什么 AUC 稳定不代表校准没问题？该怎么做？
q_en: Why does a stable AUC not mean calibration is fine, and what should you do?
why: AUC 只看相对排序——把所有概率同比例拉高，排序不变、AUC 不变，但每个概率都错了。数据漂移后重训的模型常「排得对但概率偏」。所以要在主指标旁边同时查校准（Brier score、可靠性图），不能只盯 AUC。
why_en: AUC only measures relative ranking, so uniformly inflating probabilities leaves ranking (and AUC) unchanged while every probability is wrong; check calibration (Brier, reliability diagram) alongside the primary metric.
options: AUC 稳定就一定校准良好，不需要额外检查
概率同比例偏移 AUC 不变，须并行查校准
校准问题只能靠提高 AUC 来解决，两者是同一件事
只要重训就会自动校准，漂移不影响概率刻度
options_en: A stable AUC guarantees good calibration, so no extra checking is needed.
A uniform probability shift leaves AUC unchanged, so check calibration alongside it.
Calibration issues are fixed only by raising AUC; the two are the same thing.
Retraining auto-calibrates, and drift doesn't affect the probability scale.
optionExplanations: 排序不变而概率偏移正是 AUC 看不出的盲区，稳定 AUC 不保校准。
对；AUC 与校准可脱钩，必须并行监控校准才抓得到概率漂移。
校准与 AUC 是两个独立维度，不能靠提 AUC 解决。
漂移恰恰会破坏概率刻度，重训不自动修复校准。
optionExplanations_en: Unchanged ranking with shifted probabilities is exactly AUC's blind spot; stable AUC doesn't ensure calibration.
Correct — AUC and calibration decouple, so monitor calibration in parallel to catch probability drift.
Calibration and AUC are independent dimensions; raising AUC won't fix calibration.
Drift precisely corrupts the probability scale; retraining doesn't auto-fix calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测概率与二元结果差的平方的均值，越低越好，衡量校准与准确度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Brier score is the mean squared difference between predicted probabilities and binary outcomes; lower is better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把预测概率分桶、画各桶预测值 vs 实际频率；校准好的曲线贴对角线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reliability diagram bins predicted probabilities and plots predicted vs observed frequency; a well-calibrated curve hugs the diagonal.

scenario: 你要量化一个概率分类器的校准好坏，并直观看出它在哪些概率区间偏乐观/偏悲观。
scenario_en: You need to quantify a probabilistic classifier's calibration and see visually where it's over/under-confident.
q: Brier score 和可靠性图分别提供什么？
q_en: What do the Brier score and the reliability diagram each provide?
why: Brier score 给一个标量：预测概率与二元结果差的平方均值，越低越好，便于比较。可靠性图给一张图：把预测概率分桶，画每桶「预测均值 vs 实际频率」，贴对角线=校准良好，偏离处能看出在哪个区间过/欠自信。一个量化、一个诊断。
why_en: The Brier score gives a scalar (mean squared difference between probabilities and outcomes, lower better) for comparison, while the reliability diagram plots binned predicted-vs-observed frequency to diagnose where the model is over/under-confident.
options: 两者都只给一个标量分数，无法定位偏差区间
Brier 给标量分数；可靠性图分桶定位偏差区间
Brier 是一张诊断图、可靠性图是一个数，恰好相反
两者都只衡量排序能力，与概率刻度完全无关
options_en: Both give only a scalar score and cannot localize where the bias sits.
Brier gives a scalar score; the reliability diagram bins predictions to localize the bias.
Brier is a diagnostic plot and the reliability diagram is a number — exactly reversed.
Both only measure ranking ability and are unrelated to the probability scale.
optionExplanations: 可靠性图恰恰能定位区间，不是只有标量。
对；Brier 量化、可靠性图诊断，一个便于比较、一个便于看哪里偏。
说反了：Brier 是数、可靠性图是图。
两者衡量校准/概率质量，不是排序能力。
optionExplanations_en: The reliability diagram does localize regions; it's not only a scalar.
Correct — Brier quantifies and the reliability diagram diagnoses: one for comparison, one for seeing where it drifts.
Backwards: Brier is a number, the reliability diagram is a plot.
Both measure calibration/probability quality, not ranking ability.

termDefinitions.meaning: Brier score（标量）与可靠性图（分桶曲线）配合，量化并定位概率偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration diagnostics pair the Brier score (scalar) with the reliability diagram (binned curve) to quantify and localize probability bias.

scenario: 把四类任务的默认离线指标记成一张速查表。
scenario_en: Memorize the default offline metric per task family as a cheat sheet.
q: 补全「任务类型 → 默认离线指标」的速查映射：
q_en: Complete the task-type to default-metric cheat sheet:
text: 分类不平衡→{{AUC-PR}}；搜索排序→{{NDCG}}；检索/候选生成→{{Recall@K}}；ETA/回归可解释→{{MAE}}；摘要→{{ROUGE}}；开放式生成→{{人类评估}}。
text_en: Imbalanced classification → {{AUC-PR}}; search ranking → {{NDCG}}; retrieval/candidate-gen → {{Recall@K}}; interpretable regression/ETA → {{MAE}}; summarization → {{ROUGE}}; open-ended generation → {{human evaluation}}.
why: 记住任务→指标的默认映射，面试里能秒选起点，再按数据分布/业务目标微调（如概率被消费加 log loss/校准、离群贵改 RMSE）。这是本课的核心速查。
why_en: Memorize the task-to-metric defaults so you can pick a starting point instantly, then adjust by distribution/objective (log loss/calibration when probabilities are consumed, RMSE when outliers are costly).

termDefinitions.meaning: 分类、排序/检索、回归、生成四大类，外加横切的校准，各有默认指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The task families are classification, ranking/retrieval, regression, and generation, plus cross-cutting calibration, each with default metrics.

q: 把「为一个新模型选离线指标」的推理步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the reasoning steps for choosing an offline metric for a new model:
steps: 识别任务类型（分类/排序/回归/生成）
看数据分布（是否严重不平衡）和下游是否消费概率
据此定主指标（如不平衡分类→AUC-PR、消费概率→加 log loss）
若下游把概率当真值，额外并行检查校准（Brier/可靠性图）
why: 先定任务类型缩小指标族，再看数据分布与是否消费概率，据此选主指标，最后在概率被消费时并行查校准。顺序错了（如没看分布就选 AUC）就会踩不平衡虚高的坑。
why_en: Identify the task family, then check distribution and whether probabilities are consumed, pick the primary metric accordingly, and add a calibration check when probabilities are consumed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 驱动离线选型决策的核心指标，按任务类型与数据分布确定，可配校准等辅助检查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary metric drives the offline selection decision, chosen by task type and distribution, with auxiliary checks like calibration.

scenario: 内容审核分类，正负类大致均衡，你想要一个阈值无关、便于跨模型比较判别力的指标。
scenario_en: Content-moderation classification with roughly balanced classes; you want a threshold-agnostic metric to compare discrimination across models.
q: 类别均衡、要阈值无关地比判别力，选哪个分类指标？
q_en: For balanced classes and threshold-agnostic discrimination comparison, which classification metric?
why: 用 AUC-ROC：类别均衡时它不被 TN 稀释的问题不突出，且阈值无关、能跨模型比较整体判别力，正契合内容审核这类均衡场景。若类别严重不平衡（欺诈/垃圾），才换 AUC-PR。
why_en: Use AUC-ROC — with balanced classes its TN-dilution issue is minor, and being threshold-agnostic it compares overall discrimination across models, fitting content moderation.
tradeoff: AUC-ROC（阈值无关、均衡场景比判别力） vs AUC-PR（严重不平衡时聚焦稀有正例）
whenOtherWins: 若正例极稀有（欺诈<1%、垃圾邮件），AUC-ROC 会被海量 TN 抬高虚假乐观，此时 AUC-PR 更合适。
options: F1：单一阈值下平衡精确率与召回率，但换阈值排名就会变
AUC-ROC：阈值无关、均衡类别下跨模型比整体判别力
MAE：算预测值与真实值的绝对误差，是回归指标不是分类指标
Recall@K：看 top-K 覆盖率评判别力
options_en: F1: balances precision and recall at one threshold, but the ranking shifts if you change that threshold.
AUC-ROC: threshold-agnostic, comparing overall discrimination across models under balanced classes.
MAE: averages the absolute error between predicted and true values — a regression metric, not a classification one.
Recall@K: judge discrimination via top-K coverage.
optionExplanations: F1 绑定阈值，换阈值就变，不是阈值无关的跨模型判别力比较。
对；均衡+阈值无关正是 AUC-ROC 的主场，内容审核常用它。
MAE 算的是数值误差，分类问题的输出是类别/概率，没有「预测值-真实值」这种连续误差可算。
Recall@K 是检索覆盖指标，不衡量分类判别力。
optionExplanations_en: F1 is threshold-bound and shifts with threshold — not threshold-agnostic cross-model comparison.
Correct — balanced plus threshold-agnostic is AUC-ROC's home turf, common in content moderation.
MAE measures numeric error; a classification task outputs classes/probabilities, so there's no continuous 'predicted minus true' gap to average.
Recall@K is a retrieval coverage metric, not classification discrimination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指标不依赖某个决策阈值，衡量所有阈值上的整体表现，便于跨模型比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Threshold-agnostic means the metric doesn't depend on one decision threshold, measuring performance across all thresholds for cross-model comparison.

scenario: 为生成类任务挑自动指标时，要清楚每个指标的取向与盲区。
scenario_en: When choosing automated metrics for generation, know each metric's orientation and blind spots.
q: 关于生成类评估指标，以下哪些说法正确？(多选)
q_en: Which statements about generation-evaluation metrics are correct? (multiple)
why: BLEU 精确导向、机器翻译标准、被批忽略语义；ROUGE 召回导向、摘要主流；BERTScore 用嵌入算语义、能抓同义改写。BERTScore 仍需与参考比较，并非无参考。
why_en: BLEU is precision-oriented MT-standard criticized for ignoring meaning, ROUGE is recall-oriented for summaries, BERTScore uses embeddings to catch paraphrases; all are proxies and human eval remains the gold standard for open-ended.
options: BLEU 精确导向、机器翻译标准，被批评忽略语义
ROUGE 召回导向，摘要任务主流
BERTScore 用上下文嵌入算语义相似度，能抓 BLEU/ROUGE 漏掉的同义改写
BERTScore 无需任何参考文本即可评分，因此优于所有需要参考的指标
options_en: BLEU is precision-oriented and the MT standard, criticized for ignoring meaning.
ROUGE is recall-oriented and dominant in summarization.
BERTScore uses contextual embeddings for semantic similarity, catching paraphrases BLEU/ROUGE miss.
BERTScore needs no reference text to score, making it superior to all reference-based metrics.
optionExplanations: 对；BLEU 偏精确、MT 标准、忽略语义是其著名短板。
对；召回导向让 ROUGE 契合摘要覆盖，是该领域主流。
对；语义嵌入让 BERTScore 捕捉字面漏掉的改写。
错；它算的是生成向量与参考向量的相似度，没有参考就无从算起。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — BLEU is precision-oriented, MT-standard, and famously ignores meaning.
Correct — recall-orientation makes ROUGE fit summarization coverage and dominate the field.
Correct — semantic embeddings let BERTScore catch paraphrases surface metrics miss.
Wrong — it scores the similarity between the output embedding and the reference embedding, so without a reference there is nothing to compute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器翻译，把一种语言自动译成另一种，BLEU 是其标准评估指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MT (Machine Translation) automatically translates between languages; BLEU is its standard evaluation metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工写的标准答案，BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore 都拿生成结果与它比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reference text is a human-written gold answer that BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore compare the output against.

codeSample:
from evaluate import load

scenario: 应用商店首页固定只有 5 个推荐槽位，UI 就展示这 5 个，你要评这固定窗口内的推荐质量。
scenario_en: An app-store home page has exactly 5 recommendation slots showing those 5; you evaluate quality within that fixed window.
q: 固定 UI 槽位（top-5 展示）该用哪个指标？和 Recall@K 有何区别？
q_en: For fixed UI slots (top-5 shown), which metric, and how does it differ from Recall@K?
why: 用 Precision@5：固定只展示 5 个，关键是这 5 个里有多少相关（精度），而不是「有没有把所有相关都捞进来」（那是 Recall@K，检索阶段的目标）。UI 槽位固定 → 分母固定 → Precision@K 最贴。
why_en: Use Precision@5 — with only 5 fixed slots, what matters is how many of those 5 are relevant (precision), not whether all relevants were captured (Recall@K, the retrieval goal).
tradeoff: Precision@K（固定窗口内的精度、展示阶段） vs Recall@K（整体覆盖率、检索阶段）
whenOtherWins: 若你在检索/候选生成阶段、关心「有没有漏掉相关物品」而非前几名精度，就该用 Recall@K 而非 Precision@K。
options: Recall@5：看是否把所有相关物品都捞进这 5 个
Precision@5：固定 5 个里的相关比例
MRR：只看第一个相关结果出现的位置
log loss：评这 5 个结果的概率校准
options_en: Recall@5: whether all relevant items were captured into these 5 slots.
Precision@5: the relevant fraction among the fixed 5 shown.
MRR: only where the first relevant result appears.
Log loss: score the probability calibration of these 5 results.
optionExplanations: 把所有相关都塞进 5 个既不现实也非目标，覆盖率是检索阶段的事。
对；固定槽位下 Precision@K 直接问「展示的这几个有多少相关」，最贴合。
MRR 只关心第一个，浪费了固定 5 槽的其余信息。
log loss 评概率质量，不衡量固定窗口内的推荐精度。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming all relevants into 5 is neither realistic nor the goal; coverage is retrieval's job.
Correct — with fixed slots, Precision@K directly asks how many shown items are relevant — the best fit.
MRR only cares about the first, wasting the other fixed slots' information.
Log loss assesses probability quality, not recommendation precision in a fixed window.

termDefinitions.meaning: Precision@K = top-K 中相关的比例（展示精度）；Recall@K = 全部相关中被 top-K 覆盖的比例（检索覆盖）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision@K is the relevant fraction within top-K (display precision); Recall@K is the fraction of all relevants captured in top-K (retrieval coverage).
